name: fred-mcp
what_it_holds: MCP (Model Context Protocol) server exposing FRED's 800k+ series plus ALFRED vintage data ('the numbers before revisions') as a tool interface, updated 20 Aug 2026.
why_useful: Lower priority than fredapi/alfred but notable as a very recent (Aug 2026), actively maintained wrapper if the team wants ALFRED access exposed as an agent tool rather than a library call.

name: macro-treasury-futures (point-in-time macro ML strategy)
what_it_holds: Point-in-time macro ML strategy for Treasury futures using ALFRED vintage data (CPI, payrolls, unemployment, industrial production, jobless claims -> 24 features) with leakage-safe, expanding-window Ridge regression; backtested 2020-Jul 2026 (3.85% annual return, 0.50 Sharpe, 52% hit rate). No Airbnb relevance directly but a second worked example of ALFRED-vintage + leakage-safe backtest design.
why_useful: Secondary reference implementation for vintage-aware, leakage-safe backtest design (same rationale as macro-dashboard above); the feature-engineering pattern (release-date-aligned macro surprises) could be adapted to the ABNB consumer-strength regional split workstream.

name: RJDemetra / JDemetra+
what_it_holds: R interface (and underlying Java app at github.com/jdemetra) to JDemetra+, the seasonal-adjustment software officially recommended to Eurostat's European Statistical System and the ESCB since 2015. Implements TRAMO/SEATS, X-13ARIMA-SEATS, plus nowcasting, temporal disaggregation, and benchmarking utilities. EUPL-1.2, 503 commits, 55 stars.
why_useful: This is literally the tool that produces the ONS/Eurostat seasonally-adjusted series and revisions we're trying to reason about; useful if we need to re-run or understand how Eurostat's tour_ce_omr platform-nights series (already held) gets seasonally adjusted/revised, or to build our own vintage-consistent seasonal adjustment of any series we pull point-in-time.

name: public-market-data
what_it_holds: Small but functional Python/Airflow/Postgres pipeline that ingests FRED data (currently just one JSON endpoint implemented; BCB/SEC EDGAR planned) while preserving three timestamps per observation (reference date, publication date, collection date), explicitly 'so backtests never see a future revision.' MIT, 6 commits, 12 tests/92% coverage, 0 stars -- very new/small project.
why_useful: A working minimal reference implementation of exactly the point-in-time ingestion discipline the CLAUDE.md rule #2 demands (vendor + timestamp per value); could be read as a design pattern even if not adopted wholesale, though it's early-stage and only covers one FRED endpoint so far.
